candidates.title: Agent swarms are the next scaling frontier for AI. For years, we’ve scaled intelligence by training larger models and giving them more time to think. But there’s another dimension: running many agents in parallel, exploring different approaches, challenging each other, and working together on solutions that no single agent could easily discover. OpenAI has already demonstrated the potential of this approach with breakthroughs in mathematics. Until now, experimenting with agent swarms yourself required building complicated orchestration infrastructure. Starting today on Replit, spinning up a swarm of agents is just one prompt away. Excited to see what people discover when we make collective machine intelligence programmable by anyone.

candidates.title: devin bots are multi-agent teams done right: - always on, proactive (but tuned for ROI) - own outcomes not tasks (but can collab w others) - manages teams of subagents (and reviews itself) - available everywhere (call text slack whatever hello @interaction) - consistent reporting thru interactive artifacts aka devinapps not long chats (HTML is all you need™ @trq212) this is the preview that @walden_yan gave at AIE. i've been trialing them for a week and i've been able to hand over my AEO, QA, cross-platform app porting, personal admin automation, and video editing work (also simultaneously moving from local agent worktree hell to cloud because ofc this is all cloud based thank god) hyped concepts this replaces: - /goal - "ultracode" / "ultra mode" - "loop engineering" - "agent to agent" - "agent swarms" - AI employees (see below) my main aha moment is that you don't want "AI Employees", we do not have agi yet and you will just fail if you overpromise/overexpect. what you want is the "just" the next level of abstraction above single tasks, and the overwhelming consensus I've had talking to everyone at the frontier of agents (yes incl cog competitors) is agent managers that own outcomes. incidentally, as an employer of humans it's also how i distinguish between someone who "has agency" (owns a problem area, finds issues and researches/brings solutions not problems) and who doesn't (only does precisely what i asked, not proactive, doesn't come up with suggestions i didn't think about). guess which one i value more lol. if youre a startup, reminder that Devin for Startups offers 65k in credits. apply via clanker
